title: Flooring Calculator
description: Calculate how much flooring material and how many boxes you need, including a waste allowance.

formula.summary: Room area is increased by a waste percentage to cover cuts and mistakes, then divided by each box's coverage to get the number of boxes to buy.

variables.meaning: Extra material percentage to cover cuts, mistakes, and future repairs

examples.title: 15ft × 12ft room, 10% waste, 20 sq ft per box

faqs.question: How much waste factor should I use?
faqs.answer: 10% is standard for a simple rectangular room laid straight. Use 15% or more for diagonal layouts, herringbone patterns, or rooms with many alcoves and cuts.

faqs.question: Should I buy extra boxes for future repairs?
faqs.answer: It's a good idea to keep one extra box from the same dye lot for future repairs, since flooring colors can vary slightly between production runs purchased later.

seoContent.heading: Why waste factor is essential for flooring
seoContent.body: Almost no room is a perfect rectangle that uses every plank or tile with zero cuts - closets, doorways, and room shape irregularities all create offcuts that can't be reused elsewhere. Building in a waste factor before calculating box counts avoids a frustrating mid-project trip back to the store.

seoContent.heading: Rounding up to whole boxes
seoContent.body: Since flooring is sold in sealed boxes covering a fixed area, this calculator always rounds the final box count up to the next whole box - buying a partial box isn't an option, and having one extra box on hand is far better than coming up short.
